chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
No hair or nail is to be touched from the deceased, and if anything falls from him, then place it in his shroud.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person whose body is being prepared
key_terms.سَقَطَ: fell off or became detached from the body
key_terms.شَعْرٌ: hair of the deceased, which should not be removed
key_terms.ظُفُرٌ: nail of the deceased, which should not be cut or taken
key_terms.كَفَنِهِ: his shroud, in which any fallen part should be placed

ai.seo_question: What should be done if hair, nails, or something else falls from the body of the deceased before burial?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the handling of the deceased before burial. It instructs that neither hair nor nails should be removed from the dead body, and if any part falls off, it should be placed within the kafan.
